The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} places enormous weight on its rituals, which bolster morale, reinforce sect doctrine, and often serve as tests of a vampire's strength and endurance.

Kinds of Rituals

@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} ritual falls into three groups: the Auctoritas Ritae (high rites, practiced sect-wide and observed by every Sabbat vampire), the Ignoblis Ritae (low rites, which vary from pack to pack — see the companion Sabbat Low Rites (Ignoblis Ritae) journal), and the informal customs each pack develops on its own and which shift over time.

Performing the Rites (Optional Priest Mechanics)

These rules are entirely optional — Storytellers who prefer to keep things simple can just use the standard tests associated with each rite below. For groups who want priestly skill and Path rating to matter:

  • When a priest leads a rite, she makes a Social Challenge against a number of Traits equal to the number of participants. If a bishop or higher-ranked priest leads lower-ranked assistants, each assistant adds one Trait to the lead priest's Social total.
  • Tie: participants get no bonus or penalty.
  • Priest succeeds: everyone adds one Trait per level of the priest's Path rating to their own totals for tests directly associated with the rite (e.g., the Physical total for jumping the bonfire during a Fire Dance, but not an unrelated psychic-link attempt).
  • Priest fails: make two Simple Tests. If the priest wins at least one, the rite proceeds normally. If she wins neither, all participants suffer a one-Trait penalty on related tests. The priest may instead cancel the rite, which automatically inflicts the Negative @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference.JournalEntry.St7uVm2DqK4nRy8X]{Status} Trait Unfaithful — removable only by successfully performing two more Auctoritas Ritae.

Auctoritas Ritae

Every Sabbat vampire practices these rites; their universal exercise binds the sect together.

The Binding

Performed publicly on the winter solstice as a sect-wide reaffirmation of oaths, traditionally near water (a beach, riverbank, waterfall, or at least a fountain). The ceremony opens with a recitation of the group's version of the Sabbat credo, then almost always rolls into a Vaulderie and a separate oath to protect the sect's secrets to Final Death. Founded packs host visiting nomadic packs where they can arrange safe passage. Major war efforts often launch from the Binding.

System: The Vinculum ratings of all participants increase by one (maximum 10) and remain elevated for the following month.

The Blood Bath

Performed by sect leaders to confirm a vampire's appointment to a bishopric or higher office. Each attendee steps forward, kneels, offers praise or confidence, and contributes blood to a common vessel (the leading priest goes first, then other sect leaders, then everyone else). The recipient responds to each in turn, then bathes in the pool; all participants drink from it afterward. The priest may consecrate the pool as a Vaulderie. Fervent Sabbat often refuse to fully recognize a leader who never underwent a proper Blood Bath.

System: Each participant contributes at least one Blood Trait. If the pool is consecrated as a Vaulderie, resolve it using the Vaulderie system below.

The Blood Feast

A formal, predatory banquet, often paired with other rites. For several nights beforehand, a hunting party (an honor to be chosen for) gathers human (and occasionally non-Sabbat vampire) prey, delivering captives alive and as unharmed as possible. On the night itself, the prey is arranged and the presiding official dedicates the feast to the Sabbat (sometimes preceding it with a Sermon of Caine), then draws first blood before the guests feed. Tradition calls for a minimum of one vessel per three participants.

System: The priest's opening blessing doubles the potency of the consecrated vessels' blood as it's drawn: each Blood Trait drawn from a vessel becomes two Blood Traits, though it still only occupies one Blood Trait's worth of capacity for the drinker (allowing vampires to temporarily exceed their generational blood pool limits). Any doubled Traits left unspent by the end of the third night after the Feast collapse back into single Blood Traits.

Creation Rites

The formal admission of a new Sabbat member, distinct from (and following) the mortal-killing "shovel party" embrace. Recruits remain on probation — subject to destruction for disobedience or disloyalty — until they complete the Creation Rites, which can take days, weeks, or (under strict leadership) years. A priest brands the initiate's forehead with a flaming brand while leading her in an oath of allegiance to her pack leader, the chain of command, and Sabbat principles. The priest follows the branding with a Vaulderie, after which prior blood bonds are broken and replaced by the Vinculum. Packs often add their own supplemental celebrations (gang-style initiations, formal presentations, etc.).

System: The branding requires the recruit to succeed at a two-Trait Rötschreck test. A recruit who panics gets one more chance, at a substantial stigma for cowardice; failing a second time means immediate destruction.

Some bishops form entire new packs at once via a special Creation Rite: each prospective member is drained and buried as in a shovel party and must dig free, winning (rather than just winning-or-tying) two of three Simple Tests against the Storyteller, with Physical Traits spendable for retests as usual. When (and if) every member of the pack-to-be emerges, their designated priest brands himself and the others and leads a group Vaulderie. Because this process risks losing members outright, bishops in active war zones or undermanned cities discourage it.

The Festival of the Dead (Festivo Dello Estinto)

A weeklong, sect-wide celebration occupying the second week of March, second in scale only to the Grand Ball. The presiding priest declares it open with a single instruction — Revel — and normal disputes are set aside for the duration; nomadic packs come into town to join their urban brethren. Each night typically includes a Blood Feast and a Vaulderie. Events vary widely: Fire Dancing, Book of Nod reenactments, themed hunts, and grim competitions in efficient (or creatively inefficient) killing. Archbishops and bishops award victors the right to draw first blood at the next Blood Feast, sometimes an on-the-spot promotion; a sufficiently appalling failure can mean demotion or becoming the next Blood Feast's vessel.

System: Resolve individual competitions as the Storyteller sees fit — this rite is more about roleplaying than number-crunching. Festival events involving mortal victims may require additional Storyteller-run mortal characters.

Fire Dance

A priest may call a Fire Dance whenever the pack needs morale; bishops often hold one just before a War Party, drawing together all the packs about to fight. No one is forced to participate, though packmates rarely tolerate a refusal. The convening priest lights a bonfire away from mortal eyes; participants drum, chant, and circle the flames, working into a trance before leaping through one at a time.

System: Approaching the fire requires a Courage test against two Traits (the trance state lowers the normal difficulty). Actually jumping through requires a Static Physical Challenge against five Traits; the Storyteller may raise the difficulty for showier maneuvers, which can earn bonus Social Traits for the rest of the night if successful. Every vampire who voluntarily leaps gains a bonus Courage Trait for the rest of the night and the following three nights (this bonus can exceed the normal Virtue cap of 5).

Games of Instinct

Ceremonial competitions of physical, mental, and social prowess, treated as a religious act akin to the ancient Olympic games — vigorous and often bloody, but never pointless cruelty for its own sake. A priest presides, blesses participants, and sets the terms.

System: Mechanics vary by the specific game. Universally, the winner of a Game of Instinct gains a one-Trait bonus to one Ability she used during the game, lasting two weeks of game time; this benefit applies to only one Ability at a time no matter how many Games a vampire enters. Example Games include Capture the Ductus (two packs compete to present the other's leader to the priest; inflicting Final Death on a participant forfeits the game), The Rat Race (armed mortals are hunted unarmed through a maze-like space), Rousing the Beast (digging up and destroying a shovel-party victim, who regains one Trait per turn and fights at half wound penalties), and The Spire (a barehanded climbing race up a tall structure, requiring a Simple Physical Test roughly every 10 feet at a difficulty of 6+ Traits for easy surfaces up to 12+ for sheer walls).

Grand Ball (Palla Grande)

The Sabbat's year-end celebration, held on All Hallows' Eve. Attendance is not optional; nomad packs converge on the nearest city holding one. The presiding priest prepares incense burners mixing herbs and chemicals to weaken mortal willpower and induce mild hallucination, contributing a Blood Trait of her own to each. The public first half resembles a lavish festival or rave; the private second half is a Blood Feast, followed at midnight by a ritual reenactment of Cainite legend or history. The night culminates in the ranking bishop or archbishop receiving a Blood Bath (mortal blood and a Vaulderie cup combined), followed by a final frenzied dance.

System: Participants gain the normal benefits of the Blood Feast and the Blood Bath, and fully replenish their Willpower. Each participant must contribute at least one Blood Trait to the incense burners (more is permitted). The Blood Bath's recipient may make a Mental Challenge against any other participant; on success, she may use any oracular powers that target possesses (such as Auspex or applicable Thaumaturgical Paths) as her own for the night, seeing random, symbolic glimpses of the coming year rather than gaining fine control.

Monomacy

When a dispute between Sabbat becomes irreconcilable, Monomacy — ritual one-on-one combat, traditionally to Final Death though any terms can be agreed in advance — provides the ultimate resolution. It is a genuine rite, not a right any vampire can simply claim: the pack priest must formalize it. A challenger presents her claim to the priest and the target simultaneously; the priest judges whether the dispute warrants Monomacy and either presides or appoints a substitute (if the priest is the challenged party, the ductus presides, or refers the matter to another pack's priest).

The defender is not obligated to accept — though declining costs @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference.JournalEntry.St7uVm2DqK4nRy8X]{Status}, since onlookers assume cowardice or a guilty secret. When challenger and defender belong to different packs, a bishop should technically arbitrate, though in practice the priest of a mutually acceptable third pack often handles it instead. The challenger sets the time and place; the defender sets weapons and conditions, and may request the duel be fought only to first blood (with the loser facing exile instead of death) — though doing so costs the defender respect regardless of outcome. The priest declares the duel begun and finished, and only proof of cheating justifies voiding it afterward. The victor claims first pick of the loser's possessions (excluding diablerie unless the priest specifically sanctioned it as a term of the contest); leftovers go to the loser's packmates and any other claimants.

System: All standard Mind's Eye Theatre combat rules apply during a Monomacy no matter how "anything goes" the fiction describes it; the rite calls for very little additional mechanical adjudication beyond the combat itself.

Monomacy and the Vinculum

  • If you hold a Vinculum rating of 6+ toward your intended opponent, you must burn one Willpower Trait just to initiate the Monomacy.
  • Whenever a challenger loses a bout within a Monomacy, she must spend one more Willpower Trait to continue the contest (whether or not she burned Willpower to start it). The defender, obligated to accept the challenge, pays nothing.
  • If you're punishing a packmate toward whom you hold a Vinculum of 6+ and another packmate objects, the matter is resolved with a Social Challenge; if you lose, you must burn a Willpower Trait to continue the punishment.
  • The Vinculum's general restriction against acting harmfully against someone you're bound to (see Vaulderie, below) is waived specifically for an approved Monomacy.

Sermons of Caine

Vampires who hold Caine as inspiration gather to hear teachings from the Book of Nod and discuss their relevance to the pack's situation; in some packs the priest always delivers the sermon, in others members take turns. A Vaulderie often follows. The Book of Nod is not a single fixed text but a mass of fragments, and packs argue constantly — sometimes violently — over the truest reading.

System: This rite needs no real mechanics. Storytellers who want one may call for Performance tests to gauge how effectively a speaker makes her point. Regular exposure to Sermons of Caine might raise a participant's Sabbat Lore, up to one or two levels below that of the pack priest. This is primarily a roleplaying occasion.

Vaulderie and Vinculum

The single most important Auctoritas Ritae: every participant becomes bound to every other, more intimately than an ordinary blood bond, and the bonds shift constantly rather than settling into one static hierarchy. Only a presiding priest, using ritual tools dedicated to the purpose, can make the rite work — the same actions performed by someone not recognized as priest produce no mystical effect. The priest cuts herself, drains Blood Traits into the cup, and passes it to each participant, who contributes as many Traits as they choose (contributing only one looks suspicious; contributing five or more without cause looks like a power grab). The ductus must contribute at least one Blood Trait per participant, generally more than anyone else, and is expected to leave at least one Blood Trait of her own remaining. Attempting to substitute someone else's blood from a hidden source causes the cup to erupt, spilling everyone's contribution and forcing the rite to restart — the offender typically faces swift destruction.

The priest mixes the contributed blood with a ritual invocation, then drinks and offers a blessing to each participant as the cup is passed; each participant draws back as many Blood Traits as they put in.

Vaulderie Procedure (Trait/Card System)

  1. Each participant writes her name on an index card per Blood Trait contributed to the cup (a physical chalice usually can't hold enough actual cards).
  2. The priest's player mixes the cards together with appropriate ritual flourish.
  3. Each participant draws back the same number of cards she contributed.

Vinculum Rating

Each participant ends up with a Vinculum rating of 1–10 toward each other participant; ratings are not symmetrical (Andrew might hold a 6 toward Bettina while she holds only a 1 toward him).

  • First Vaulderie with a given vampire: Vinculum rating of 1 toward every other participant, plus one more for each of that individual's cards drawn.
  • Subsequent Vaulderies: make a Static Challenge of your current Vinculum rating toward a given participant against a total of (1 + number of that participant's cards you drew this time). Lose: Vinculum rises by one. Tie: unchanged. Win: you may make two Simple Tests; winning both lowers the Vinculum by one (otherwise unchanged). A Vinculum toward a fellow participant can never fall below 1. Willpower and Traits cannot be spent for retests on this challenge.
  • Optional simplified version: each player makes one Static Challenge for her Vinculum rating toward everyone in the rite at once, using the highest total of Blood Traits she drew from any single individual. This sacrifices some of the inter-personal intrigue the granular system provides.

Vinculum ratings do not fade with time — only the Vaulderie itself can lower one. Packs that perform it regularly build very deep, lasting ties.

Vinculum Restrictions

  • Destroying a vampire to whom you hold any Vinculum rating at all: spend two Willpower Traits.
  • Acting against the interests (non-lethally) of someone you hold a Vinculum of 3+ toward: spend one Willpower Trait.
  • Acting against the interests of someone you hold a Vinculum of 6+ toward: spend two Willpower Traits.
  • The only exception to all of the above is an approved Monomacy.

When Vinculum ties to multiple people conflict, the character makes an Extended Challenge of her Willpower against each relevant Vinculum rating (adding two to her Willpower for the individual she personally favors most); whoever accumulates the most successes wins her loyalty in that moment. As a simpler alternative, she may just follow whichever Vinculum rating is numerically higher, especially with a gap of two or more.

Breaking a Blood Bond via Vaulderie

The Vaulderie can gradually unmake an ordinary blood bond. A bound vampire seeking release must contribute at least six Blood Traits to a Vaulderie, reducing herself to one Blood Trait remaining. Doing this three times completely breaks one blood bond to a specific regnant (and generates very strong Vinculum ratings to the rite's other participants in the process).

War Party

Multiple packs compete to bring down a designated non-Sabbat elder, with the eventual diablerist gaining all the normal benefits of diablerie. A bishop or higher declares the War Party after identifying a worthwhile target; preparations usually include a Fire Dance, a Sermon of Caine, and a Blood Feast or Vaulderie. The War Party's chief asks each ductus the ritual question, "Do you come freely to war, and do you take up this noble cause, never resting until the blood of our enemy is spilled?" Each answers "We do!" A ductus may withdraw her pack, at the cost of ridicule (and an open invitation for packmates to call Monomacy against her on the spot). Almost any tactic is fair game during the hunt itself, including heavy collateral damage. Tradition awards the kill to whichever pack member's fangs reach the victim first, regardless of who did the most work bringing her down.

System: The vampire who actually diablerizes the target receives all the usual benefits of diablerie. The entire winning pack receives the temporary Status Trait Martial, lasting until the next War Party, Grand Ball, or Festival of the Dead. Exceptionally prominent targets (Methuselahs and the like) can earn the victors permanent Status instead.

Wild Hunt

The Sabbat's ultimate sanction against treachery — the sect's answer to the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}'s blood hunt. A priest (usually the highest-ranked in the area, and ideally with her superiors' backing, or she risks the same punishment herself) calls the Wild Hunt, after which all loyal sect members must hunt down the traitor and anyone, Cainite or mortal, he may have confided in. Vampires who destroy a Wild Hunt target before interrogation risk Final Death themselves. Preparatory rites (Vaulderie, often Fire Dancing) are performed solemnly rather than festively. Captured traitors are interrogated and tortured for confession and to trace the leak; once confirmed, torture becomes straightforward punishment. Vampiric collaborators face torture as well, while mortal contacts are usually killed quickly. The traitor is finally staked and burned on a consecrated pyre while a priest recites the Book of Nod's Chronicle of Caine, followed by a Vaulderie to re-seal the pack's bonds.

System: Some regions allow the Ignoblis Ritus of Contrition to let a Wild Hunt target make amends instead of facing destruction, at Storyteller discretion — appropriate for minor offenses. More serious treachery should bring more serious (potentially fatal) consequences; character death should never be arranged lightly, but shouldn't be avoided when it's genuinely earned either.
